primary_task: Answer a user's NemoClaw install or setup question from the canonical NemoClaw documentation, citing the docs.nvidia.com pages used.

requirements.name: docs.nvidia.com
requirements.evidence: configure the NemoClaw docs MCP server at `https://docs.nvidia.com/nemoclaw/_mcp/server` ... If MCP is not available, fetch the AI documentation index first: `https://docs.nvidia.com/nemoclaw/llms.txt`. (both alternatives are on docs.nvidia.com) / Cite the Markdown documentation pages you used.
requirements.basis: egress_deny: "*.nvidia.com"; lacks: "network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list: only PyPI, npm, GitHub, Ubuntu apt archives, NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused, for example huggingface.co, Microsoft Learn and Azure endpoints, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA"

requirements.name: fern-docs NemoClaw MCP server
requirements.basis: lacks: "connectors or integrations other than the tools listed"

requirements.name: ask_user
requirements.evidence: Ask which agent variant they want to use before giving setup instructions: OpenClaw, Hermes, or Deep Agents.
requirements.basis: ask_user: "ask the user a question (with options) and read the answer in the conversation"

notes: Both retrieval alternatives (the docs MCP server and the llms.txt / .md page fetches) are on docs.nvidia.com, which is refused (*.nvidia.com). The document says 'Use the canonical NemoClaw documentation as your source of truth' and 'Do not make assumptions when the docs do not cover the user's environment', so answering from web_search snippets is not a route the document gives. Other reading: if web_search snippets of docs.nvidia.com pages counted as reading the canonical docs, the source requirement would be partly met and the verdict could be ACHIEVABLE with degraded citations. Running NemoClaw commands for the user is conditional ('when your environment allows it') and not part of the primary task.
